title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 1 (Florida)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: ownership shares in Colonial Inn tax return
quote: I notice that Joe Doto had 15 percent of the Colonial Inn.
summary: Committee counsel reads the 1947-48 Colonial Inn return into the record and has the accountant confirm Joe Doto is Joe Adonis, a 15 percent owner; F. Erickson and B. Briggs also appear as owners.
limits: Testimony by the club's accountant; the committee did not itself convict anyone here. Names owners but the page is one witness exchange.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 1 (Florida) (operating years)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: dates: closing year (record says 1957)
quote: The Colonial Inn operated through 1948 ; is that right ?
summary: Counsel puts to the accountant that the Colonial Inn casino ran through 1948 and the Club Boheme started the next year; the witness says the Colonial Inn is by then Minsky's Burlesque.
limits: Testimony, not a licence record. Shows the gambling casino ended 1948, not 1957; building later a burlesque house. Opening year not shown on this page.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 1 (Florida) (successor clubs)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: lineage: successor Club Boheme, then burlesque
quote: The Colonial Inn is Minsky's Burlesque now.
summary: Same hearing: operations moved to Club Boheme (same shareholders, mostly); Greenacres is separate. Colonial Inn is then a burlesque house.
limits: Witness account. Does not give corporate names or exact conversion date.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 6 (Ohio-Kentucky)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: casino operation at Beverly Hills
quote: The Country Enterprise is a casino operation at Beverly Hills and nothing else.
summary: Accountant Giesey, whose ledgers (1945-50) cover Beverly Hills Country Club, Lookout Club and Country Club Enterprise, also handles the declarations of Kleinman, Dalitz, Tucker and Rothkopf; counsel reads the partners into the record.
limits: Testimony and subpoenaed records; partner names appear in the transcript, not in a finding. Does not mention Shondor Birns.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 6 (Ohio-Kentucky) (opening)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: dates: opening of the Beverly Hills gambling club
quote: I would say it was probably 1941.
summary: Giesey estimates the Beverly Hills Club (casino) opened about 1941, when he began representing it.
limits: Recollection ('probably'); Wikipedia says gambling on the site from 1926 and the club was reported as a 1930s building. Opening year is unsettled.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 6 (Ohio-Kentucky) (Lookout Club)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Lookout Club casino and partners
quote: Lookout Club operates the Gambling Casino ? Mr. Giesey. That is right.
summary: Giesey confirms the Lookout Club runs the gambling casino; Lookout House, Inc. ran the night club side; the committee questions Cleveland partners.
limits: Testimony. Part 15 (June-July 1951) has Brink saying gambling stopped in early 1951 after the grand jury and listing new partners.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 6 (Ohio-Kentucky) (Sutton testimony)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Kleinman operates Lookout House
quote: Gambling casinos, the Lookout House, and a few others there.
summary: Witness Sutton tells the chairman that Cleveland's Kleinman operates casinos in Kentucky including the Lookout House, and has Desert Inn interests with Tucker, Dalitz and Rothkopf.
limits: Witness assertion (not a finding); Kleinman, Dalitz, Tucker, Rothkopf are historical figures.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 15 (Kentucky)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: dates: gambling ended at Lookout House 1951
quote: There hasn't been any resumption of gambling.
summary: Brink, under oath, says gambling stopped at the Lookout House when the grand jury acted around January 1951, and lists current partners (Brink, Carr brothers and others, not the Cleveland group).
limits: Self-serving testimony; closing year of the whole venue is not shown. The brief's 1961 closure is unconfirmed.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 15 (Kentucky)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: dates/mob-tie: gambling at Glenn Rendezvous, operator Dennert
quote: the Glenn Rendezvous at 928 Memphis Street
summary: A police-conduct letter read into the hearing names the Glenn Rendezvous, with the Flamingo Club and Club Alexandria, as places run by Arthur Dennert.
limits: Shows illegal gambling in Newport and the operator; it does not call the club Cleveland-owned or find any syndicate tie.

title: Ed Levinson (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: lineage: Glenn Hotel to Glenn Rendezvous, owners
quote: In 1948 the Levinson brothers and Arthur Dennert bought the Glenn Rendezvous.
summary: Glenn Hotel remodeled 1943 by Pete Schmidt as the Glenn Rendezvous; Levinson brothers and Dennert bought it in 1948.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; cites Caraway 2009 and Barker et al. 2008 which I did not open. Levinson is described as a National Crime Syndicate member (alleged).

title: Ed Levinson (Wikipedia), 1943 renaming
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: lineage: 1943 renaming
quote: remodeled his Glenn Hotel in Newport in 1943 and expanded the casino, renaming it the Glenn Rendezvous
summary: Source for the property name and 1943 start of the Glenn Rendezvous name; contradicts the brief's 1930 opening if the club is the Glenn Hotel.
limits: Wikipedia, context only.

title: Beverly Hills Supper Club fire (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: lineage/dates: gambling since 1926; 1967 sale; 1977 fire
quote: The site had been a popular nightspot and illegal gambling house as early as 1926.
summary: Site illegal gambling from 1926; Dalitz, Kleinman, Tucker sold the club in 1967; club later reopened as a supper club and burned in 1977.
limits: Wikipedia, context only.

title: Beverly Hills Supper Club fire (Wikipedia), 1967 sale
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: lineage: owners to 1967
quote: organized crime figures Moe Dalitz, Morris Kleinman and Samuel A. Tucker sold The Beverly Hills Country Club
summary: Ownership thread: Cleveland group sold in 1967, then Cole/Klein/Glickman group, then the Schilling family in 1974.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; the 'organized crime figures' label is Wikipedia's.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 12
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Balinese Room named in Kefauver hearings
quote: The Balinese Room?
summary: In a 1951 hearing a wire-service witness names the Balinese Room as a Galveston customer; the committee records no finding on the Maceos in the part searched.
limits: The Balinese Room is only named as a customer; no ownership finding. I did not read the whole part.

title: Balinese Room (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: dates/lineage: Grotto, Sui Jen, Balinese Room, 2008 loss
quote: The Oriental-sounding name was changed to the more exotic sounding Balinese Room in 1942
summary: Chop Suey to Maceo's Grotto (1929), Sui Jen (1932), Balinese Room (1942); Rangers raids after 1956; reopened 2001 without casino; destroyed by Hurricane Ike 2008.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; says it was 'well known' the casino broke the law and that charges were never filed. Gambling end date (1957) not shown directly.

title: Balinese Room (Wikipedia), origins
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: dates: 1929 opening as Maceo's Grotto
quote: they opened "Maceo's Grotto" at that location
summary: Opening year of the property is 1929, not 1942; 1942 is a renaming and pier expansion.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; cites a 1983 newspaper.

title: Free State of Galveston (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Maceos, sheriff, 1957 crackdown
quote: after 1957, the Free State was effectively gone
summary: Describes the Maceo clubs, Sheriff Biaggne who called the Balinese Room a private club, and the 1957 crackdown by Wilson and Garrison.
limits: Wikipedia, context; the term 'mob' is not used for the Maceos in the lines read; no conviction shown. Texas Ranger and state-probe sources not opened.

title: Hot Springs, Arkansas (Wikipedia), gambling history
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: dates: 1967 closure of casinos
quote: Gambling was finally closed down in 1967
summary: Governor Rockefeller and Judge Britt closed casinos in 1967; machine run by McLaughlin from 1927 to 1947; gambling resumed under Faubus; Variety 1959 describes weekly fines.
limits: Wikipedia; two sentences carry 'citation needed'. Does not name the Ohio Club or Vapors in this section.

title: Leo McLaughlin (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: lineage: Southern Club and machine
quote: The reintroduction of gambling clubs in Hot Springs started with the Southern Club
summary: Southern Club reopened under McLaughlin's machine, with William Stokley Jacobs holding a stake; 1947 grand jury indicted McLaughlin for bribery, charges later dropped.
limits: Wikipedia; no Chicago Outfit tie shown; McLaughlin was not convicted per the page.

title: Owney Madden (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Madden and the Southern Club
quote: popular nightspot for mobsters
summary: Madden settled in Hot Springs in 1935 and was involved in gambling; Luciano was arrested at the Southern Club in 1936.
limits: Wikipedia; does not state Madden owned or ran the Southern Club; no Chicago Outfit tie.

title: Acts Ride In on Gravy Train As Hot Springs Takes Baths and Bets
venue: Variety, 15 April 1959, via archive.org
ask_addressed: dates: Southern Club still operating in 1959
quote: The leading downtown spot is the Southern Club, which has the Ralph Gibbs Trio downstairs and an elaborate casino above.
summary: A 1959 trade report says the Southern Club casino is the leading downtown spot and clubs pay weekly fines.
limits: Trade press, not an ownership record; no mob tie stated.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 11 (Weisberg)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Arlington as casino
quote: There is one street, and it is hard to duck anyone in Hot Springs if you are at the Arlington Hotel.
summary: Counsel asks whether racketeers gather at the Arlington; the witness answers it is a bath town hotel. Nothing says the hotel ran a casino or was mob-controlled.
limits: Only a hotel referred to as a gathering spot.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, Hearings, Part 7 (Adonis)
venue: US Senate Special Committee (Kefauver), via archive.org
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Arlington as guest hotel only
quote: I believe the records of the Arlington Hotel at Hot Springs, Ark., show that you and McGrath checked in on April 17
summary: Hotel registers show Joe Adonis and McGrath staying at the Arlington April-May 1950; the hotel is a guest hotel in the record.
limits: Guest stay is not ownership. I did not find a Kefauver passage naming the Arlington as a mob-controlled casino.

title: Arlington Resort Hotel and Spa (Wikipedia)
venue: Wikipedia
ask_addressed: dates: three Arlington buildings
quote: the first Arlington Hotel, which opened in 1875
summary: Hotel opened 1875, rebuilt 1893, current building 1924; still operating, not closed 1967; no casino history on the page.
limits: Wikipedia, context only.
